_retired_note: Qwen3-ASR-1.7B was removed from this platform on 2026-09-08 — service, image, weights, provider and configuration. This file is kept ONLY as historical evidence of what was measured while it ran. It configures nothing: no service reads it, no test requires it, and the model it describes is no longer installed. Numbers below are from 2026-09-08 on spark-2 and are not reproducible without reinstalling that engine.
_about: Phase 0 baseline for the FROZEN Qwen3-ASR implementation. Every number here was measured on 2026-09-08 against the live engine; nothing is copied from documentation or estimated. Fields that could not be measured are null with a stated reason, never filled in with a plausible value.

runtime.why_derived_image: vLLM ships Qwen3ASRForConditionalGeneration but the audio decode path is behind the vllm[audio] extra, which the published image omits.

hardware.head: spark-1 (NVIDIA GB10)
hardware.why_the_worker: The head carries the main model's TP rank 0, the vision router, the embedder, OCR and the reranker. Measured 2026-09-08: spark-1 70.01 GB GPU memory allocated, spark-2 40.44 GB.

measured_how: Direct HTTP to the live engine, chat path, production decoding settings (temperature 0.0, max_tokens 1024). Audio is the model authors' published English sample (asr_en.wav, 15.1 s, 48 kHz mono), resliced by looping to the requested length, plus generated digital silence.

decoding.note: These are orchestrator/app/asr.py's settings verbatim. A run at different settings is not comparable.

resource_baseline.interpretation: 10.14 GB corresponds to --gpu-memory-utilization 0.08 of the GB10's 128 GB unified memory (~10.24 GB). Weights are ~4.4 GB on disk; the remainder is the engine's KV/activation reservation, which vLLM claims up front and does not release.
resource_baseline.model_load_time_reason: Not measured: the engine has been up for hours and measuring it requires a restart, which Phase 0 forbids.
resource_baseline.vram_before_load_reason: Not measured: would require stopping the running engine.
resource_baseline.cpu_memory_reason: Not measured: the container runs on the worker and this session has no SSH host key for it.

latency._note: 5 repeats per length, warm engine, sequential. Median reported. Spread was under 4 % at every length, so these are stable.
latency.first_request_note: First call of the session at 15 s of audio. Indistinguishable from the warm median (990 ms) — the engine was already loaded, so this is NOT a cold-start measurement.
latency.percentile_reason: Not reported. 5 samples per length is enough for a median and nowhere near enough for a p95; a percentile computed here would be a number people quote and nobody can defend.
latency.fallback_path_note: /v1/audio/transcriptions at 15 s: 1.002 s against the chat path's 0.990 s. The two paths cost the same; the chat path is preferred because it also reports the identified language.

concurrency._note: 15-second clips, issued simultaneously, one engine. Throughput is seconds of audio transcribed per second of wall clock.
concurrency.interpretation: Four concurrent clips finish in the wall-clock time of one — the engine batches them. Eight cost 13 % more wall clock than one. ASR_MAX_CONCURRENT=4 per engine is therefore not protecting the ASR engine; it protects the CHAT model that shares the GPU.
concurrency.cost_to_chat_model_reason: Not re-measured. Measuring it means loading the production chat model while people are using it, which Phase 0 forbids. docs/VOICE.md records -5.8 % decode at 4 concurrent and -10.1 % at 8, measured 2026-09-04.

quality._status: NOT MEASURED — no benchmark corpus exists yet.
quality.reason: benchmarks/asr/corpus/ contains a manifest TEMPLATE and no audio. WER and CER require human-recorded clips with reference transcripts across the eight categories, and none exist in this repository. The scoring harness (benchmarks/asr/evaluate.py) is written, verified end to end against the live engine, and waiting on audio.

behavioural_checks._note: What COULD be established without a reference corpus. These are behaviours, not accuracy scores.
behavioural_checks.silence_language_handling: The engine emits the literal token 'None' as the language on silence. app/asr.normalise_language rejects it (not in SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES) and returns null rather than inventing a language. Correct, and worth keeping when a candidate model replaces this one.
behavioural_checks.determinism_note: Latency spread under 4 % across 5 repeats at each length; transcripts were byte-identical across repeats at temperature 0.

known_limitations: No WER or CER: the benchmark corpus has no audio. This is the single biggest gap before any candidate model can be compared.
No Hindi, Indian-English or Hinglish measurement of any kind — the three categories this deployment was chosen for.
No cold-start / model-load time: measuring it requires restarting the engine.
No p95: 5 samples per length cannot support one.

Latency was measured with looped WAV rather than real WebM/Opus recordings. The engine decodes both through PyAV and docs/VOICE.md reports them identical, but this specific run did not re-verify that.
The reference audio is the model authors' own published sample, which a model author may have trained on. It is fit for latency and plumbing, and unfit for accuracy.

discrepancies_found.what: docs/VOICE.md reports 60 s of audio at 1.85 s / 32.4x real time.
discrepancies_found.assessment: The documented 60 s row is not reproducible. The 5 s, 15 s and 30 s rows all reproduce within 8 %, and 15.9x at 60 s is the value consistent with them — real-time factor flattens with length, it does not double. The documented figure looks like a clip that was shorter than 60 s rather than a faster engine.
discrepancies_found.action: Recorded, not corrected. Phase 0 does not edit documentation; source and runtime win, and this is the evidence.

discrepancies_found.what: docs/VOICE.md says the engine holds 'about 6 GiB while warm'.
discrepancies_found.measured: 10.14 GB (9.44 GiB) for the ASR VLLM::EngineCore process on spark-2.
discrepancies_found.assessment: 6 GiB is close to the manifest's approximate_loaded_weight_bytes (6.44 GB) — the weights. The process actually holds the full --gpu-memory-utilization 0.08 reservation, which is ~10.24 GB of the GB10's 128 GB. Both numbers are real; they measure different things, and the documented one understates the footprint a second engine would cost a node.

discrepancies_found.what: ASR_BASE_URLS names two engines; only one answers.
discrepancies_found.measured: http://192.168.9.68:30006/v1 (worker) responds in 2.4 ms. http://172.17.0.1:30006/v1 (head) refuses the connection, and no ASR container runs on the head.
discrepancies_found.assessment: Dictation still works. RoutedProvider sorts by in-flight count and both start at zero, so the healthy worker is tried first and the dead head is only reached under load, where it costs one failed connection and a 20 s stand-down. Not a fault in the code — a fleet that was started with --all-nodes and is now running one engine.
discrepancies_found.action: Recorded. Not changed: altering ASR_BASE_URLS would change the running configuration, which is what Phase 0 froze.

discrepancies_found.what: The repository has no .env, but the running orchestrator has ASR_ENABLED=true and a full ASR configuration.
discrepancies_found.measured: ls .env -> no such file. docker exec orchestrator env -> 11 ASR_* variables set.
discrepancies_found.assessment: The running container holds configuration that no longer exists on disk. ASR_ENABLED defaults to false and scripts/asr.sh writes the .env that turns it on, so re-running ./techsara up today would start the orchestrator with voice input DISABLED and silently lose the feature. The container is the only copy of this configuration.
discrepancies_found.action: Recorded and flagged as the highest-priority operational risk found in Phase 0. Not changed: creating a .env is a production configuration change.

still_needed_before_candidate_evaluation: Human-recorded benchmark audio: >=10 clips in each of the eight categories, WebM/Opus mono from a browser MediaRecorder, with verbatim reference transcripts.
A re-run of benchmarks/asr/evaluate.py against this frozen engine once that audio exists, to fill in the WER/CER this file leaves null.
A decision on whether cold-start time matters enough to justify one controlled restart of the ASR service.
